title: How Supervolcanoes Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain supervolcanoes and how they differ from ordinary volcanoes: they are defined by a huge magma chamber and reservoir rather than a mountain, have no strict scientific definition, and are measured by magnitude, intensity, and the Volcano Explosivity Index. They cover past eruptions (Toba, Fish Canyon Tuff, Krakatoa, Vesuvius), the Campi Flegrei volcano under Naples, and Yellowstone's magma system, its past eruptions, its eruption risk, and the incubation process. They also cover the 1815 Tambora eruption and the year without a summer that inspired Frankenstein. The episode ends with a listener email about Dennis Barry, the Robert Mapplethorpe obscenity trial in Cincinnati, and Barry's later work at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

segments.title: Opening banter and supervolcano basics
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter, then contrast supervolcanoes with ordinary volcanoes: a supervolcano is marked by a huge magma chamber and reservoir, often with a caldera or hot spot, and can change global climate.

segments.title: Past super eruptions: Toba, Campi Flegrei, Fish Canyon Tuff
segments.summary: They discuss the Toba eruption about 74,000 years ago and its possible ice age effects, the Campi Flegrei volcano under Naples and its raised threat level, and the Fish Canyon Tuff eruption in Colorado about 20 million years ago.

segments.title: Defining supervolcanoes and measuring eruptions
segments.summary: The hosts explain that supervolcanoes have no strict definition and are compared by magnitude and intensity. They compare eruption rates of Vesuvius and super volcanoes, and describe the Volcano Explosivity Index.

segments.title: Krakatoa's loud eruption
segments.summary: Krakatoa's 1883 eruption is described as the loudest sound ever recorded, with its shock wave circling the Earth four times. About 36,000 people were killed.

segments.title: Yellowstone's magma system and past eruptions
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Yellowstone hot spot and its track, the magma chamber and reservoir estimates, and Yellowstone's past eruptions: Huckleberry Ridge, Mesa Falls, and Lava Creek.

segments.title: Yellowstone eruption risk, incubation, and effects
segments.summary: They discuss what a Yellowstone eruption could do, the USGS probability estimate, ground doming and heating, the incubation process of magma buildup, and the Tambora eruption and the year without a summer that inspired Frankenstein.

segments.title: Listener mail: Cool uncle and the Mapplethorpe trial
segments.summary: Listener Katie Barry writes about her uncle Dennis Barry, director of the Contemporary Arts Center in Cincinnati, who was arrested and tried on obscenity charges over the Robert Mapplethorpe exhibit The Perfect Moment, and was acquitted. He later became founding director of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts mention a future episode on the PMRC and give social media and email contact information, then sign off.
